sections.title: SURVEY BASIS
sections.body:
**Archive interval:** Three pedestrian traverses and one stationary overnight run

**Instrumentation:** Independent quartz timebases, fluxgate magnetometer, VLF receiver, barometric recorder, and paired environmental loggers

**Study boundary:** A coded riparian reach and its ordinary vehicle-access corridor; property and geographic identifiers are retained separately.

sections.title: OBSERVED VARIANCE
sections.body:
**Timing residual:** Two oven-controlled quartz timebases on independent batteries and loggers accumulated same-direction offsets of 42 to 96 milliseconds while passing through a roughly 220-metre survey band. Raw oscillator counts contained no missing samples. Both units returned to their established drift rates after removal but retained the accumulated offset.

**Field correlation:** Each onset coincided with a 1.7-to-2.3-nanotesla departure in the local magnetic trace. No matching change appeared on the stationary reference package.

**Repeatability:** Direction and walking speed changed the duration of the observation but not its mapped entry and exit points. Across three traverses, the two timebases agreed on boundary crossing within 3 milliseconds.

sections.title: INTERPRETIVE LIMITS
sections.body:
**Ordinary explanations tested:** Receiver coupling, temperature compensation error, buried utility material, and an unrecorded ferrous source were evaluated in bench and control-route trials. None reproduced the shared step change or the fixed entry and exit boundary.

**Interpretive limit:** The record establishes a location-bound discontinuity in the instrument timebases, not a change to civil time or a biological effect. The coupling mechanism remains unknown.

sections.title: DISPOSITION
sections.body:
**Finding:** Repeatable, location-bound timebase discontinuity corroborated by two isolated instruments and a local magnetic excursion

**Action:** Maintain the reach as a passive comparison site. Later work requires three independent timebases, a continuously operating remote reference, and pre-registered boundary criteria.

**Personnel control:** No exposure limitation is indicated beyond ordinary remote-field procedures.
